hypotheses.title: Linear Normalized Breakeven Asymmetry with 5-Day Velocity
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Direct structural optimization of Batch 151 Candidate 2 (46ec7888, which achieved Sharpe 1.14 and Sub-universe Sharpe 1.03 with zero self-correlation). In the ratio formulation (call - close)/(close - put), when price approaches put breakeven the denominator approaches zero, creating outlier volatility and inflating turnover to 40.59%. Normalizing the net difference ((call - close) - (close - put) = call + put - 2*close) by spot price provides a mathematically stable percentage metric. This eliminates near-zero denominator singularities to compress turnover while preserving the fast 5-day dealer momentum that generated high predictive Sharpe.
confounders: Sudden corporate action adjustments altering strike matrices
Short-term gamma pin risk during expiration week
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha underperforms if linear asymmetry fails to distinguish between high-volatility and low-volatility underlying equities.

hypotheses.title: Breakeven Asymmetry 10-Day Percentile Rank Channel Breakout
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Direct acceleration of Batch 152 Candidate 2 (3ebfe7dd, which achieved Sharpe 1.02 and Sub-universe Sharpe 0.90 with 29% turnover). Tightening the time-series percentile lookback from 20 days to 10 days (ts_rank(ratio, 10)) captures rapid dealer inventory adjustments and institutional call accumulation twice as fast, while maintaining smooth, bounded [0, 1] ranking that suppresses discrete noise spikes.
confounders: Post-earnings implied volatility crushes resetting percentile channels
Thin liquidity on out-of-the-money option contracts
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha underperforms if 10-day percentile breakouts reflect transient retail gamma squeeze rather than institutional repositioning.

candidates.expression: 0.60 * group_rank((ts_backfill(call_breakeven_20, 60) - close) / (close - ts_backfill(put_breakeven_20, 60) + 0.01 * close), subindustry) + 0.40 * group_rank(ts_rank((ts_backfill(call_breakeven_20, 60) - close) / (close - ts_backfill(put_breakeven_20, 60) + 0.01 * close), 10), subindustry) - 0.10 * group_rank(ts_delta(close, 5) / close, subindustry)
candidates.rationale: 20-day breakeven ratio level + agile 10-day time-series rank breakout

hypotheses.title: Orthogonal Domain Synergy: Options Gamma Asymmetry & Fundamental Cashflow Efficiency
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Applies Tulchinsky's All-Domain Pairing Architecture (Chapter 15) by synthesizing two completely virgin datasets in the portfolio: options dealer gamma positioning (option9) and fundamental cashflow efficiency derivatives (model16). Both have 0 approved alphas in the database. Operational cash generation provides a persistent, low-turnover fundamental anchor, while options gamma breakeven asymmetry captures agile upside dealer rebalancing. Because the drivers are orthogonal, turnover is substantially dampened, amplifying the Fitness metric.
confounders: Discrepancies between fundamental reporting cycles and options expiration cycles
Severe liquidity shocks affecting broad equity markets
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if market rewards unprofitable growth stories over cashflow-efficient equities during options rallies.

candidates.rationale: Orthogonal synthesis of 20-day options breakeven asymmetry and fundamental cashflow operational efficiency
